perspective:
From John Atcitty’s available perspective:

- He knows his own background: Alaska Native, Heavy Equipment Operator, middle-school education. He also knows Beverly as a colleague at the community center and knows/perceives that she has a doctorate.
- John set up the equipment for a joint class demonstration and hoped it would meet Beverly’s expectations.
- He heard Beverly say she admired how he handles machines, that education isn’t just about degrees, and that it’s about what you can do with what you know.
- After Beverly praised his machinery expertise, John thanked her and suggested a workshop combining theory and practice.
- He heard Beverly say she loved the idea, that his practical skills were invaluable, and that they could create something special together.
- After a successful collaboration, John worried he might not always meet the high standards they had set. He told Beverly this honestly.
- He heard Beverly appreciate his honesty, suggest setting realistic goals, and say their combined efforts—not perfection—make projects successful.
- After their frank discussion, John said he was glad they talked and that being able to be open mattered to him. He heard Beverly say she respected his openness, trusted his judgment completely, and wanted transparency to continue. From this, John believes she values his honesty and sees him as a reliable partner.
- Encouraged by their collaborations and perceived mutual respect, John proposed a larger community-wide event to showcase their projects.
- He heard Beverly call the idea fantastic, say it was the perfect way to demonstrate their impact, and agree to start planning.

John does not have access to Beverly’s private thoughts, feelings, or narrator-only information beyond what she said, did, or what he inferred from their interactions.
